hook: Repurposing is not copying the same paragraph everywhere.
caption: Start with one useful idea, then choose the angle that fits each format. A process may work as a short demo; the reasoning behind it may work better as a text post. Keep the meaning, change the explanation. What source are you working from this week?
call_to_action: Comment with the source type you repurpose most.

hook: One source. Five useful angles. No copy-paste carousel.
caption: Slide 1: choose the core promise. 2: find a how-to. 3: find a common question. 4: find a surprising lesson. 5: give each angle its own format. Save this framework for your next recording.
call_to_action: Save this and map one source into five angles.

hook: Stop turning every clip into the same post.
caption: Script: 0-2s: 'One source, different jobs.' 2-10s: show a transcript with three highlighted ideas. 10-22s: label them how-to, FAQ, lesson. 22-30s: 'Match each idea to a format; keep the meaning intact.' On-screen captions throughout.
call_to_action: Comment with one format you want to test.

hook: A good repurposing brief starts with one sentence.
caption: Write the source's central promise in one sentence. Then ask: what can someone do, understand, or decide after seeing this? Build each post around one answer. This keeps the content useful even when separated from the original.
call_to_action: Save the prompt and use it on your next source.

hook: Three highlights hiding in your last recording.
caption: Script: show a waveform. Mark one step-by-step moment, one audience question, and one surprising lesson. Text overlay: 'Three angles, one source.' End: 'Which one deserves its own post?' Use original screen graphics and subtitles.
call_to_action: Pick one highlight and draft its hook today.

hook: A clip needs context before it needs captions.
caption: Script: 0-3s: show a contextless quote card. 3-12s: add the question the speaker was answering. 12-25s: explain the takeaway in one sentence. 25-35s: show the clip with captions. Lesson: make the idea understandable on its own.
call_to_action: Try adding the original question above one clip.

hook: A useful edit can be shorter without being shallower.
caption: Cut repetition, not the reasoning. Keep the example that makes the lesson concrete, and remove setup that the audience does not need. Read the draft aloud: if the point still lands, the edit is doing its job.
call_to_action: Share one editing rule you use.

hook: The 3-question test for a standalone clip.
caption: Can a viewer tell what question this answers? Is the key context included? Is there one clear takeaway? If any answer is no, add context before publishing. Alt text: Three questions for checking a clip: question, context, takeaway.
call_to_action: Save this checklist for your next edit.

hook: One clip, one takeaway. Here is the cut.
caption: Script: show a long sentence, remove the tangent, keep the example and conclusion. Overlay each cut as it happens. Voiceover: 'The edit should make the idea easier to follow, not change what the speaker meant.'
call_to_action: Use this test on one clip and compare drafts.

hook: A content calendar is a set of decisions, not a pile of dates.
caption: For each slot, know the audience question, the format that serves it, the person reviewing it, and the signal you'll learn from. If one of those is missing, the date alone will not make the post easier to produce.
call_to_action: Audit one upcoming calendar slot with these four questions.

hook: Turn one audience question into a useful mini-series.
caption: 1: write the exact question. 2: answer in one sentence. 3: show a concrete example. 4: cover one common exception. 5: invite the next question. Avoid stretching one answer into several thin posts.
call_to_action: Save this sequence for your next FAQ.

hook: Your FAQ answer has a built-in video structure.
caption: Script: display a question. Say the short answer first. Give one example. Name one exception. Close by asking which related question to cover next. Keep each beat on screen as it is spoken; add accurate captions.
call_to_action: Write down one question you hear repeatedly.

hook: The opening line should make a promise the post keeps.
caption: A strong hook is not just surprising; it tells the right reader why to continue. Draft the takeaway first, then write an opening that sets the same expectation. If the body cannot deliver, change the hook.
call_to_action: Rewrite one hook after drafting the body.
target_metric: Dwell and substantive replies; baseline first

hook: Make a tutorial easier to follow with one visual cue.
caption: Script: demonstrate one task while a numbered label marks each step. Keep the cursor or hands visible, avoid tiny interface text, and pause between steps. Close with a recap card. Add subtitles and check contrast before posting.
call_to_action: Try numbered visual cues in your next walkthrough.

hook: A before-and-after is only useful when you show the decision.
caption: Script: show a rough draft and its edited version. Pause on the change. Explain why the change improves clarity, then mention what meaning stayed the same. Use your own draft or licensed material; do not expose private client work.
call_to_action: Explain one edit decision in your next tutorial.

hook: A simple quality review catches more than typos.
caption: Review in this order: factual accuracy, audience usefulness, context, accessibility, rights, CTA, tracking. Fix the earliest failure first; polishing a caption cannot rescue an unsupported claim.
call_to_action: Save this review order for your next batch.
target_metric: Saves and document completion; baseline first

hook: Before publishing: claim, consent, contrast, captions, click.
caption: A quick five-part preflight: are claims checked, people and assets approved, text readable, video captioned, and link tested? Alt text: Five checks before publishing a creator post.
call_to_action: Use the five checks on your next post.

hook: Accessibility is part of the edit, not the cleanup.
caption: Script: show captions being corrected, not just auto-generated. Check names, timing, and line breaks. Describe important visuals in speech or text. End: 'A viewer should not need perfect audio to get the point.'
call_to_action: Check captions on mute before publishing.
target_metric: Caption accuracy and retention; baseline first

hook: Measure the action the post asked for.
caption: If the CTA asks people to save a checklist, clicks are not the only useful signal. If it asks them to visit a page, track outbound clicks and completed actions. Choose the metric before publishing so the result can teach you something.
call_to_action: Name one signal for your next CTA before posting.

hook: A tiny UTM naming habit saves future guesswork.
caption: Use a consistent source, medium, campaign, and asset name. Example: source=instagram, medium=social, campaign=2027_growth, content=asset_id. Test the tagged link and confirm analytics receives it before scheduling.
call_to_action: Save the naming pattern and adapt it to your campaign.

hook: Reach tells you who had a chance to see it. Then what?
caption: Script: show a simple funnel: reach, meaningful engagement, outbound click, completed action. Explain that each step answers a different question. Compare like with like and avoid calling correlation proof of causation.
call_to_action: Pick one funnel step to improve this month.

hook: A low-performing post still gives you a useful question.
caption: Was the audience wrong, the opening unclear, the example too abstract, or the format hard to consume? Change one variable in the next attempt and keep the rest steady enough to learn from the result.
call_to_action: Write one hypothesis before changing the next post.

hook: Test two openings without changing the lesson.
caption: Script: present hook A and hook B for the same tutorial. Keep audience, body, length, and CTA consistent. Explain that this is a directional test, not proof from one post. Use platform-native experiments where available.
call_to_action: Draft two hooks for one idea and choose a fair test.

hook: One post is not a verdict on an idea.
caption: Script: show three dots representing repeated tests. Voiceover: 'Audience, timing, hook, and distribution all vary. Look for patterns across comparable attempts, record the context, and keep conclusions proportional to the sample.'
call_to_action: Record context with your next result.

hook: Your audience questions can become an editorial backlog.
caption: After answering a question, note the underlying job: choosing a tool, finding time, explaining a concept, or measuring progress. Group related jobs and plan a series that solves one job from several angles.
call_to_action: Collect three audience questions this week.
target_metric: Useful replies and question collection; baseline first

hook: A thoughtful comment can reveal the next useful post.
caption: 1: notice the question behind the comment. 2: check whether others ask it too. 3: answer without exposing private details. 4: invite correction. 5: turn the answer into a post only when it helps more people.
call_to_action: Use a recurring question to plan one post.
target_metric: Saves and relevant replies; baseline first

hook: A strong series has a repeatable promise.
caption: Script: show episode cards with the same title pattern. Explain the repeatable promise in one line, vary the example each episode, and invite viewers to request the next problem. Keep each episode useful on its own.
call_to_action: Name a recurring creator problem for a series.
target_metric: Returning viewers and comments; baseline first

hook: A creator workflow should make review easier, not add ceremony.
caption: Use a short brief: audience, one takeaway, evidence, format, CTA, reviewer. Keep approval steps proportional to risk. Product claims and personal data deserve careful review; a routine spelling fix does not need a committee.
call_to_action: Try the six-field brief on one upcoming post.
target_metric: Saves and workflow adoption; baseline first

hook: Can someone understand your post with sound off?
caption: Script: play a silent tutorial with clear on-screen steps, then show captions and a concise ending card. Keep critical meaning in text or visuals. Check that overlays are readable on a phone.
call_to_action: Preview one video muted before it goes live.
target_metric: Muted-view retention and saves; baseline first

hook: Your next month's plan starts with what you learned this month.
caption: Script: review the top posts by the metric each one intended to move. Identify one repeated audience question and one format worth repeating. Keep a note of what you would change. End with a simple next-month experiment.
call_to_action: Review your results and choose one next experiment.
target_metric: Review completion and qualified clicks; baseline first
